lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Launch and planning: mapping a support network by role

objective: Learners map their own support network by role rather than by name (who could I ask about money, school, health, or a big decision) so they have a private, personal reference for who to turn to, without disclosing anyone's identity to the lesson itself.
scenario: The learner privately identifies, for each of five life-role categories, at least one real person in their life who could help, but records the map using only relationship or role labels (such as 'a school counselor' or 'an aunt') rather than full names, keeping the map for their own private reference.
safetyNotes: Full names, addresses, phone numbers, or other identifying details are never entered into this task sheet; use role/relationship labels only (e.g., 'a neighbor,' 'a school counselor').
If a category has no one the learner can think of, it is acceptable and useful information to record honestly as a gap rather than inventing a name.
This map is for the learner's own private reference; nothing here requires sharing who any specific person is with anyone else to complete the lesson.
materials: paper or a private notes document

tasks.directions: Before mapping, think about the five categories: money questions, school/career questions, health questions, a big decision, and an emergency.

prompts.text: Which of the five categories comes to mind fastest for you, and which feels hardest to think of someone for?

tasks.directions: For each of the five categories, record a role/relationship label for someone you could ask, or record it honestly as a gap.

prompts.text: I filled in a role label or an honest 'no one yet' for the money-questions category.
I filled in a role label or an honest 'no one yet' for the school/career-questions category.
I filled in a role label or an honest 'no one yet' for the health-questions category.
I filled in a role label or an honest 'no one yet' for the big-decision and emergency categories.

tasks.directions: Identify the one gap you most want to close and think of one realistic first step.

prompts.text: Name the category with the biggest gap (using a role label, not identifying anyone), and write one realistic first step you could take to build support there.
Now that this is written down, would you actually remember to use it in a real situation? What would help you remember?

remediation: If the learner leaves most categories blank without engaging honestly (not even writing 'no one yet'), reteach by modeling that an honest gap is a valid and useful answer, not a failure, then have the learner revisit each blank category and either name a role or explicitly record it as a gap.
extension: Have the learner add a second person for each category where they could, so the map has a backup, not just a first choice, and write one sentence on why having a backup matters for at least one category.
